extracted.intended_audience: lawyers, military administrators, War Department officials, and state National Guard/adjutant general offices
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of legal standards and administrative rules governing what organizations and persons qualify as militia or Organized Militia, and the entitlements, limitations, reimbursements, and authorities applicable to militia service, encampments, details, and joint maneuvers under the acts of January 21, 1903 and related statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State may not create militia exempt from Presidential call without Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: A State cannot, without the consent of Congress, create a military force which shall form a part of its militia and at the same time be exempt from being called forth by the President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age limits for militia membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The militia is limited to able-bodied men between the ages of 18 and 45 under the act of January 21, 1903 (32 Stat. 775); a company of cadets composed of boys under 18 cannot be considered militia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cadet corps of minors are therefore ineligible to receive benefits provided for militia under that act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary organizations not part of National Guard not eligible for federal stores
rubrics_metrics.description: A purely voluntary organization which forms no part of the National Guard of a State is not entitled to receive stores of any kind from the United States under the act of January 21, 1903.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership in the Organized Militia/National Guard is prerequisite for supplies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal militia appropriations limited to Organized Militia
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no authority of law by which any part of the Federal appropriation for the militia may be employed to cover the expenses of sending a unit which is not a part of the Organized Militia of the State to public events (e.g., expositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units not part of Organized Militia cannot be funded from militia appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cadet corps at educational institutions not Organized Militia
rubrics_metrics.description: A cadet corps (e.g., at a university) was not contemplated by the general militia act of January 21, 1903 and does not constitute a part of the Organized Militia of the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insular police and native groups not automatically militia
rubrics_metrics.description: Insular police (e.g., Porto Rico) and certain indigenous groups (e.g., Alaska Indians) that lack the legal status of militia are not entitled to share in federal appropriations made for the support of the militia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial militia establishment requires Congressional action
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment of an Organized Militia in a Territory is a legislative act beyond the power of the governor; Congress must take steps to establish a Territorial militia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale of arms/ammunition to Indian Territory forbidden
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress has expressly forbidden the sale of arms or ammunition in the Indian Territory; there is no authority of law for issuing United States rifles and munitions for organizing militia there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterans/retired lists and honorary commissions not part of Organized Militia
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers and enlisted men transferred to a 'National Guard Veterans' list or who hold 'honorary' commissions retain rank/uniform but are not part of the Organized Militia and are not eligible for certain positions (e.g., State disbursing officer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Congress may impose age limits as condition of federal assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress has authority to impose reasonable limits of age upon commissioned officers as a condition precedent to assistance in money and war material which it affords to the Organized Militia of the several States; this does not invade State appointing power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal allotment may be conditioned on conformance to Regular Army physical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government may condition its allotment to the militia upon conformation of the National Guard to the physical standards of the Regular Army and can deny pay to a militia officer on the ground that he is not physically fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for militia enlistment governed by state law
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualifications for enlistment in the militia depend on the laws of the States; federal enlistment prohibitions (e.g., dishonest prior service disqualifier in Army law) do not necessarily preclude state militia enlistment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncitizenship is not barred by federal law from state militia enlistment; state statutes control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncitizen/nonresident students may enlist in State militia
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no enactment of Congress restricting service in the militia of a State to citizens of that State; noncitizen or nonresident students of a college within that State may enter a contract of enlistment which would be effective if called into U.S. service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired Regular Army personnel may accept militia positions under conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired soldier of the Regular Army may accept a position (e.g., sergeant major) in the Organized Militia without affecting his retired status; enlistment of retired Regular officers in the National Guard is not per se unlawful though its expediency may be questioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retired officers detailed to militia are not placed upon the Regular Army active list; various statutes govern pay and allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlistment in Regular Army does not automatically discharge National Guard membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The enlistment of a member of the National Guard in the Regular Army does not operate as a discharge from the National Guard; the enlistee remains liable to penalties under State law for failure to obtain a militia discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appointment to an Academy (e.g., West Point) likewise does not discharge militia enlistment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlements for militia officers attending U.S. military schools (Section 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an officer of the Organized Militia attends and pursues a regular course of study at any military school or college of the United States upon recommendation and authorization, he shall receive the same travel allowances and quarters, or commutation, to which a Regular Army officer would be entitled, and commutation of subsistence at the rate of one dollar per day while in actual attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance must be authorized by President and recommended by governor/commanding officer; must 'pursue a regular course of study' to retain entitlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia officers attending U.S. military schools are not in U.S. military service
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers of the Organized Militia attending military schools under the statute are not thereby in the military service of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at schools generally restricted to officers on active list
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance by militia officers at such schools is by implication restricted to officers on the active list; a retired officer is not authorized to attend as a student under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to travel/mileage depends on authorization and residence
rubrics_metrics.description: A militia officer so attending is entitled to the same travel allowances as a Regular officer would have been entitled to if detailed; however, if the officer lives in adjoining city and merely travels daily, he is not entitled to mileage for travel to/from the post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garrison school attendees entitled to heat and light; commutation rights subject to definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Militia officers attending garrison schools and receiving commutation of quarters are entitled to heat and light (act of March 3, 1909); however commutation of quarters payment statutes are restricted to 'officers of the National Guard' (Organized Militia) and do not apply to retired officers or certain civilians made eligible under other sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an officer is absent for entire course period, he fails to 'pursue a regular course of study' and loses right to quarters or commutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on supplies and purchases for militia officers attending schools
rubrics_metrics.description: A militia officer attending a U.S. military school is not entitled to draw stationery or forage, is not authorized to purchase clothing from the Quartermasters Department, but may purchase fuel at contract rates at posts where schools are established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriations for clothing are intended to clothe the Army, not to furnish clothing at cost to persons not connected with the Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: No allowances during absence or ordinary/sick leave while attending school
rubrics_metrics.description: A militia officer attending a military school is not entitled to any allowances while absent from the school or on ordinary leave or sick leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanding officers should authorize absence for state duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A commanding officer of a post at which militia officers are attending a garrison school should recognize their obligations to the Organized Militia of their States by authorizing their absence to perform duties (e.g., participating in an inaugural ceremony) to which their organizations had been detailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement of travel expenses regulated by statute; excess charged to State allotment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reimbursement of officers for travel expenses is regulated by the act of June 12, 1906 and supplemented by June 22, 1906; traveling expenses incurred in excess of the regular mileage allowance incurred in the execution of militia inspection shall constitute a charge against the allotment of the State on whose behalf the journeys are undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If orders carry no allowances (for example, a Regular officer assigned to temporary duty with the National Guard with only mileage law allowances), there is no relief for excess expenditures except by Congressional action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain travel expenses (telephone, typewritten reports) not reimbursable under mileage act
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of June 22, 1906 is restricted to reimbursement 'for the actual excess of expenses of travel'; expenses such as telephone use may not be reimbursed under that act and may need to be charged to other appropriations (e.g., Quartermaster appropriation); typewriting inspection reports may be charged to contingencies appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired Regular officers assigned to militia: statute and pay rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired officers of the Regular Army are assigned to duty with the militia under the act of March 2, 1903 (not under section 20 of Jan. 21, 1903); the act establishes pay and such an officer is entitled to increased pay and allowances thus authorized from the moment he reports to the governor of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The act of April 23, 1904 and its modification by June 12, 1906 further govern assignments and set pay maxima (e.g., maximum pay/allowances of a major).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty with militia not per se mounted duty; entitlements clarified
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty with the militia is not per se mounted duty; retired officers detailed to militia are subject to several limits (e.g., not entitled to certain mileage depending on grade), and they may hold civil office and accept State compensation unless prevented by State law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War authority to assign retired officers to staff duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of April 23, 1904 provides the Secretary of War may assign retired officers to 'staff duties not involving service with troops' (e.g., inspecting the Organized Militia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of retired officer on duty extends from reporting until relief; leave authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The status of duty which attaches to a retired officer assigned to duty with the Organized Militia should, in absence of exceptional circumstances, apply for the entire period between his reporting for duty and his relief; a governor cannot grant leave of absence to such an officer—only the War Department can.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlisted Regular Army men detailed to Organized Militia (Section 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlisted men of the Regular Army may, upon application of the governor, be detailed for duty in connection with the Organized Militia; such enlisted men are entitled to pay, commutation of rations, quarters (number of rooms as per Army Regulations), and heat and light where authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs of maintenance for such detailed enlisted men are a charge against Army appropriations and cannot be paid from funds accruing to the States under section 1661.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutation of rations may be paid in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Commutation of rations may lawfully be paid in advance to an enlisted man of the Regular Army placed on detached service with the Organized Militia of a State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of Philippine Scouts to territorial militia unlawful
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of the restriction in the law authorizing Philippine Scouts, the assignment of an officer of Philippine Scouts to duty with the militia of a Territory would be unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor discretion on portion of militia in State camp (Section 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 14 uses 'such portion' in describing what part of the National Guard shall participate in a State camp of instruction; it is within the governor's discretion to determine what portion shall engage in field or camp service for instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: No statutory restriction on place of State field or camp instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 14 contains no restriction as to the place where 'actual field or camp service for instruction' shall take place; the governor's discretion controls but passage through another State requires that latter State's consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Army post for State instruction not automatically Regular Army participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Location of a National Guard organization in camp on an Army reservation for purposes of instruction does not classify the camp as participation in Regular Army encampments, maneuvers or field instruction merely because Regular officers acted as instructors; it can be the State encampment under section 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale of subsistence stores at State encampment
rubrics_metrics.description: At a State encampment held under section 14, subsistence stores may be sold to officers and the sale will be regarded as a sale to the State under section 17; selling price should be cost to the United States plus 10% for transportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursing officer under section 14 not entitled to commutation of quarters in camp
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of the disbursing officer under section 14 is limited to field or camp service and quarters are not furnished to officers for this kind of service; commutation of quarters cannot be paid to such a disbursing officer for time spent in camp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on rations credit for disbursing officer purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: A disbursing officer who purchased rations under section 14 may take credit for the amount actually spent if the average does not exceed the value of the Regular Army ration; if the average exceeds that value, credit is limited to the value of the Regular Army ration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation hire and other encampment expenses chargeable to State allotment
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs such as hiring wagons for cavalry practice marches and necessary transportation expenses (e.g., transportation of a sick militiaman home) are proper charges against the State's allotment under section 1661, while other expenditures (e.g., medical expenses en route) may not be authorized under section 14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific instances: hiring wagons = proper charge; medical attendance en route = no authority under section 14; transportation of sick violent epileptic requiring attendants = proper charge if necessary and reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crop damage claims and incidental expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment for damage to crops caused by troops during maneuvers will not lawfully be a charge against the State allotment under section 1661 and may be paid only as incidental expenses when authorized by the Secretary of War; pre-encampment leases with restoration clauses affect liability and compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement for officers' purchased transportation when properly ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: Where prior to necessities it was not possible for the disbursing officer to secure transportation, officers who purchased transportation properly ordered and actually expended funds may be reimbursed by the State disbursing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement for transportation of staff officers' horses
rubrics_metrics.description: The State disbursing officer may lawfully reimburse a mounted officer for amount expended in transporting a horse (e.g., foundered in service) from encampment back to home when the horse was used by a member of his staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funds accruing to State under encampment appropriation restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds accruing to the State under the appropriation for 'Encampment and maneuvers, Organized Militia' are subject to restrictions in sections 15 and 21 and are not available for certain uses (e.g., entertaining visiting foreign military attaches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leases for maneuvering lands create implied compensation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Leases of lands to the United States for maneuvers that deprive lessors of use and possession operate to create an implied contract for reasonable compensation for the use and occupancy for the period during which the lands were occupied; leases executed after possession may be treated as liquidation of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking rules during joint service with Regular Army
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Organized Militia and the Regular Army serve together as contemplated by statute, article 124 of war requires that no officer of the militia of a particular grade can rank any Regular officer of that grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'participation' in joint encampments and entitlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 15, 'participation' in encampments, maneuvers and field instruction of the Regular Army begins when movement from rendezvous begins and ends when troops reach return rendezvous; during this period militia are entitled to the same pay, subsistence, and transportation as Regular Army troops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation disbursement and limitation for joint encampments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sums provided in annual appropriations for joint encampments of the Regular Army and Organized Militia cannot lawfully be transferred to a State disbursing officer and must be disbursed by regularly appointed officers of staff departments of the Regular Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation procurement for militia to maneuvers follows Regular Army methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Transportation of militia forces to and from maneuvers on military reservations must be obtained in the same way and in pursuance of the same statutes and regulations that would be applied in obtaining transportation for corresponding detachments of the Regular Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire of automobiles and other transport expenditures limited by designation
rubrics_metrics.description: The hire of an automobile for transportation of adjutant general or staff officers who were not designated by the Secretary of War to take part in the joint encampment does not constitute a lawful charge against the appropriation for the joint encampment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale of subsistence stores at joint encampment to Regular Army at cost
rubrics_metrics.description: At a joint encampment participating militia may sell subsistence stores to officers and enlisted men of the Regular Army at cost prices, i.e., the same prices which are charged to Army personnel under the same circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forage not allowed under section 15 allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 15 restricts allowances to 'pay, subsistence, and transportation;' forage is not an allowance to which the National Guard becomes entitled when participating in encampments with the Regular Army.
